generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Sketching \(R,\) we have

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-5, 10, 10, -5], keepAspectRatio:true, showCopyright:false, axis: true, defaultAxes: { x: { name:'\\(x\\)', withlabel:true, label: { position:'rt', offset:[-20,15], fontSize:15, useMathJax:true, parse:false } }, y: { name:'\\(y\\)', withlabel:true, label: { position:'rt', offset:[15,-5], fontSize:15, useMathJax:true, parse:false } } }, showNavigation:true }); var p1 = board.create('point', [{#x_1#},{#y_1#}],{fixed:true}); var p2 = board.create('point', [{#x_2#}, {#y_2#}],{fixed:true}); var p3 = board.create('point', [{#x_3#}, {#y_3#}],{fixed:true}); var p4 = board.create('point', [{#x_4#}, {#y_4#}],{fixed:true}); var pol = board.create('polygon', [p1, p2, p3, p4]); var poly2 = board.create('polygon',points,{name:"Polygon 2",withLabel:true, hasInnerPoints:true, withLines:true, vertices:{visible:true}}); [[/jsxgraph]]

The equations of each of the boundaries of the region are given in the sketch.

Apply the transformation to each of the boundary equations by plugging the transformation into each of the boundary equations.

Applying the transformation to \(y={@eqn_y1@}\) gives,

\(\frac{1}{2}(v+u)=\frac{1}{2}(v-u)+{@y_intercept1@}\)

\(v+u=v-u+{@2*y_intercept1@}\)

\(2u={@2*y_intercept1@}\) therefore \(u={@y_intercept1@}\)

This boundary transform into the equation \(u={@ta1@}\)

Applying the transformation to \(y={@eqn_y2@}\) gives

\(\frac{1}{2}(v+u)=-\frac{1}{2}(v-u)+{@y_intercept2@}\)

\(v+u=-v+u+{@2*y_intercept2@}\)

\(2v={@2*y_intercept2@}\) therefore \(v={@y_intercept2@}\)

This boundary transform into the equation \(v={@ta2@}\)

Applying the transformation to \(y={@eqn_y3@}\)

\(\frac{1}{2}(v+u)=\frac{1}{2}(v-u)+{@y_intercept3@}\)

\(v+u=v-u+{@2*y_intercept3@}\)

\(2u={@2*y_intercept3@}\) therefore \(u={@y_intercept3@}\)

This boundary transform into the equation \(u={@ta3@}\)

Applying the transformation to \(y={@eqn_y4@}\)

\(\frac{1}{2}(v+u)=-\frac{1}{2}(v-u)+{@y_intercept4@}\)

\(v+u=-v+u+{@2*y_intercept4@}\)

\(2v={@2*y_intercept4@}\) therefore \(v={@y_intercept4@}\)

This boundary transform into the equation \(v={@ta4@}\)

Sketching the transformed equations gives the following region.
